exact_semantic_question: What does PASS=0 / FAIL=1 reporting mean, and is it a numeric concentration comparison?
relation_contract: binary pass/fail coding is not ordinary concentration comparison

candidate_interpretations.label: binary_wet_outcome_code
candidate_interpretations.description: 0 and 1 are categorical pass/fail codes for whole-effluent-toxicity test outcome. 0 = pass (NOEC at or above critical dilution); 1 = fail (NOEC below critical dilution). Values are entered in the DMR concentration-max field but do not represent a measured concentration magnitude.
supported_by: DMR_COMMENT_TEXT pass/fail legend on all 12 affected limit rows
final_permit.txt Part II reporting table for TEM3D/TEM6C and retest codes
9A pass=0;fail=1 unit on pass/fail limit rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR

candidate_interpretations.label: numeric_concentration_comparison
candidate_interpretations.description: Reported 0/1 values are pollutant concentrations (mg/L, %, etc.) compared numerically against LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR.
refuted_by: DMR comment explicitly defines 0/1 as pass/fail codes, not concentrations
Pass/fail parameters have no numeric LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR; companion TOM3D/TOM6C parameters carry numeric NOEC reporting separately

candidate_interpretations.label: shared_comment_different_reporting_regimes
candidate_interpretations.description: All 12 rows share the PASS=0/FAIL=1 comment at the limit-set level, but only TEM/retest parameters (8 rows) use binary 0/1 reporting; TOM3D/TOM6C/TQM3D/TQM6C (4 rows) report numeric NOEC or coefficient-of-variation values per separate permit instructions.

retained_snippets.text: Enter a "1" if the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) for survival is less than the critical dilution, otherwise enter a "0".

known_limitations: Critical dilution magnitude is not stated in the inspected structured rows; only the comparison logic (NOEC vs critical dilution) is established from permit text.

Four of twelve affected limit rows (TOM3D, TOM6C, TQM3D, TQM6C) share the PASS=0/FAIL=1 comment but are governed by separate numeric-reporting instructions; the pass/fail legend applies to TEM and retest parameters, not to those four.
Sublethal retest parameters (22418, 22419) use the same 0/1 coding in structured data; permit retest table text inspected references survival NOEC vs critical dilution for retest 1–3.
